chapter: Philadelphia, Atlantic City and the war years
title: Hearing of Pearl Harbor in a Philadelphia hotel with Basie's men
summary: Caldwell, Dickie Wells, Jimmy Rushing and Don Byas heard the news on the radio on an off Sunday.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So then, now, these three years you're in Philly --
Yeah, I was in Philly from the year
Pearl Harbor was bombed

that they call (unintelligible). Basie was in Philadelphia at that particular time, and we were -- Dickie Wells and I went around to a place called the Pet Shop, where all the musicians and performers used to go and you could buy whiskey there, you know, under the table. So it was on a Sunday, and so I was living upstairs because I was staying there, and (unintelligible) had a room on the first floor in the back. So Don said to me, said, 'Happy, why don't you come on to the back, said, we got a bottle.' 'Oh, no, Dickie and I going around to the Pet Shop, and we going to get a little snack,' and Dickie and I would buy the bottle, you know (unintelligible).

So Jimmy Rushing, was sitting there talking with Jimmy, so Dickie and I went around to the Pet shop, the Pet Shop, and we came back. So we sitting out in the lobby talking, and Jimmy Rushing, Dickie and I, so all of a sudden Don Byas came running into the lobby, hey -- hey, man, they bombed Pearl Harbor. I said, you got to be kidding.
(Laughter)

So -- he said, no kidding. It's on the radio. So we all went back there, Jimmy and I and Don, and Dickie Wells, and they was broadcasting, said, yeah, Japanese have bombed Pearl Harbor. I said, man, this is for the birds. I said no it ain't (unintelligible) for the birds. I mean we're in another war. And Don was brought the news to us (unintelligible). Everybody went
cockeyed then because didn't know nothing about the Japanese going to bomb Pearl Harbor.
(Laughter and simultaneous remarks)
Kind of a surprise.
Well, it was a surprise. I'll never forget that.
Yeah, that's funny. Well, that's right. I see you were in Philly, and the Basie band came to town.

They came to play there, you know, and they were off that Sunday, and we were all staying at Douglas Hotel (unintelligible) (and) knowing each other, and we'd just sit there and have a ball. That broke up the ball, when they came out with that the Japanese had bombed Pearl Harbor. I thought (unintelligible) forgot about the whiskey.
(Laughter)

Well, I remember hearing that too (unintelligible) you know, that the people, everybody said 'I'll be damned.' (unintelligible) It was several things happened in that war that, you know, when they happened, you couldn't quite believe them.
No, you couldn't.
(Unintelligible).
I said, Come on! man, you kidding? He said, no, So Jimmy said, oh, you gotta be-- you know how Rushing talks (unintelligible), Jimmy Russian (unintelligible). So Dickie said, let's go back and

the band, find them. I said, come on, man. Come on. So we run back there the radio was playing. Yeah, they bombed Pearl Harbor. Yakety Yakety (unintelligible). Old Bill says, I'll be damned. There you goes, Johnny, get your gun, like you got to go again, (unintelligible). We're in World War II now. You're kidding, (unintelligible). That's the way it happened. The old hotel where went silent (unintelligible).
I was there, you know, think about the Japanese -- that (unintelligible) at least for a bit.
(Simultaneous remarks)
But, of course, what they really thought was that, yeah, they thought Germany was going to finish Russia off.
That's right.
And if she had, that would have been a different thing.
(Simultaneous remarks)
Because it was very close, you know.
Very close.
Because she could have turned around and wiped England out then. But, well, so -- I mean these three years in Philly, you were sort of playing around.

'cause I Yeah, always stayed in the same hotel, and they played that Friday and Saturday night in Philly (unintelligible) maybe going back to New York that Monday because they was off that Sunday. And so we were just staying there
Sunday, staying to have a ball, just about an hour and a half ride from New York, lesser than that. And that's what happened that Sunday.
